summary: Intermittent Windows clients lose access to internal hostnames after VPN connects (PAC + split-DNS)
description: Several Windows 11 laptops report intermittent failures resolving internal *.redwood.corp hostnames immediately after establishing the corporate VPN. Affected users can browse public internet sites fine but internal services (Confluence, internal API endpoints, Grafana) return DNS errors or timeouts until VPN is disconnected and reconnected or the machine is rebooted.
impact: Multiple engineers across SF and London offices unable to reach internal developer tooling and services for short periods (5-20 minutes). Productivity impact is moderate; workaround exists but disruptive.
environment: Windows 11 Enterprise clients on corp-managed fleet; VPN client: WireGuard-based corporate client (v2.4.1) with split-tunnel enabled and a proxy auto-config (PAC) pushed via GPO. Issue observed in us-west and eu-west VPN endpoints.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot a corporate Windows 11 laptop on corp Wi-Fi (or home network).
2) Ensure PAC is applied via Group Policy (check IE/Edge connection settings).
3) Establish VPN connection to us-west endpoint using corp client v2.4.1.
4) Immediately attempt to access an internal hostname (e.g., confluence.redwood.corp or api.internal.redwood.corp).
5) Observe DNS failures or long timeouts. In many cases, access is restored after disconnecting and reconnecting VPN or rebooting the client.
observed_behavior: DNS lookup fails for internal domains; apps show 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN' or time out. 'nslookup' sometimes returns public resolver IPs instead of corporate DNS. Route table shows interface metrics where VPN interface is not preferred for certain traffic until metric recalculation or reconnect.
expected_behavior: After VPN connects, client should resolve internal *.redwood.corp names via corporate DNS servers pushed by the VPN and route internal traffic via the VPN tunnel without requiring manual reconnect/reboot.
diagnostics: Collected ipconfig /all from affected machines showing DNS suffix search list missing 'redwood.corp' until reconnect.
route print captured during failure showing default gateway still assigned to Wi-Fi adapter with lower metric than VPN interface.
Windows Event Log entries pointing to GroupPolicy refresh at VPN connect time and a race between PAC application and DNS registration.
Packet capture on client shows initial DNS queries going to public DNS (1.1.1.1) until DHCP/DNS settings from VPN propagate.
VPN server logs show successful push of DNS servers and DNS suffix but some clients report no immediate application of those settings.
investigation_notes: 03/05 10:20 - Initial report from eng #support Slack channel (see slack thread: #support: 'vpn-dns-flap-03-05').
03/05 11:00 - Reproduced on 2 Windows 11 VMs with corp image. Observed that PAC eval runs on browser startup and can override DNS behaviour for certain domains.
03/05 13:15 - Hypothesis: Race condition where Group Policy + PAC apply after VPN establishes, causing DNS suffix/search list to be temporarily empty and PAC to route internal domains incorrectly.
03/06 09:30 - Compared behavior to macOS clients: macOS applies VPN DNS and suffix immediately; issue appears Windows-specific and tied to interface metric assignment and PAC application timing.
03/06 14:00 - Tested workaround: forcing VPN interface metric lower (netsh interface ipv4 set interface X metric=10) prevented the symptom in test VM.

03/07 08:45 - Found a change in recent GPO script that sets proxy PAC via registry at user login; when PAC is re-applied after VPN connect, it triggers a WinHTTP/WinINET refresh which temporarily drops the corp suffix.
03/08 16:00 - Coordinated with Endpoint team. Confirmed corp client v2.4.1 contains a known timing bug on Windows where DNS suffix update is applied asynchronously; vendor has a fix in v2.4.2.
03/09 09:00 - Deployed temporary config change to GPO: disable reapply of PAC on network state change and pushed a client-side script to set interface metric on VPN connect as mitigation.
03/09 13:00 - Monitored for 24h; no new reports after mitigation rollout to pilot group (20 users).

root_cause: Timing/race between PAC application from GPO and asynchronous application of DNS suffixes from the VPN client on Windows 11. Client v2.4.1 did not atomically apply DNS search list and interface metrics on connect, allowing traffic to use public DNS until a reconnect or reboot.
resolution: Short-term: updated GPO to avoid reapplying PAC on network-change events and deployed an Intune script to set VPN interface metric lower on connect for Windows clients. Long-term: coordinated vendor upgrade to VPN client v2.4.2 (contains fix for DNS suffix application race). Deployed vendor update to the fleet on 2026-03-09 and monitored for 48 hours.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-09 - Rolled out v2.4.2 of corp VPN client via Intune to 100% of Windows fleet.
2026-03-09 - GPO change applied: PAC not re-pushed on network state change; documentation updated to avoid registry-based PAC reapply.
2026-03-09 - Intune script added: on VPN connect, set interface metric=10 for the tunnel adapter to prefer tunnel routes.
Post-deploy monitoring: No new internal DNS resolution reports in 72 hours across pilot and then full fleet.
follow_up_tasks: Create a KB article for Windows users describing the reconnect/reboot workaround and explaining the fix timeline.
Add a health-check to infra monitoring that alerts if >5% of Windows VPN sessions report missing 'redwood.corp' DNS suffix within 30 minutes of connect.
Review GPO scripts that modify proxy settings; migrate PAC deployment to Intune-managed configuration to avoid registry reapply race.
Postmortem note: consider vendor contract clause for patch SLAs for client-side critical fixes.
